draft.title: Protected areas
card: A protected area is land or sea set aside mainly to conserve nature. National parks protect habitats on land. Marine reserves do the same in the ocean.
Large
a bigger area can hold bigger populations and a wider range of habitats. Small populations are more at risk of dying out.
Connected
links such as wildlife corridors let animals move between areas to find food and mates, and to adapt as the climate changes.
Well managed
an area needs staff, funding and rules that are enforced. It must also deal with threats such as weeds, feral animals and poaching, which can still enter a park.
draft.remember: A protected area helps most when it is large, connected and managed well, not just when it is declared on a map.

a.q: A national park is declared, but it has no funding for rangers and feral cats and weeds spread through it. Which feature is missing?
opts: Good management
Large size
Marine protection
Wildlife corridors
a.why: Without staff, funding and action on threats, the park cannot protect its species. Size and corridors may matter too, but the problem described is that threats go unmanaged.
a.clue: Look at what is happening to the threats inside the park.

b.q: Two small reserves in a farming region each hold a few dozen koalas. Cleared paddocks lie between them. What would most improve the koalas' survival?
opts: Planting a tree corridor linking the two reserves
Fencing each reserve to keep koalas inside
Declaring a third small reserve far away
Banning visitors from entering both reserves
b.why: A corridor lets koalas move between the reserves, which links the small populations and widens their range. Fencing keeps them isolated, so it works against connection.
b.clue: The problem is the cleared land between the reserves.

b.best: Planting a tree corridor linking the two reserves

problems.detail: The clue 'The problem is the cleared land between the reserves' all but names the corridor answer. It gives the answer away instead of prompting the student to apply the idea of connection.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate and each has one clear right answer. The clue for question b nearly gives the answer away and should be made less direct.
